NeutrinoAPIKeyCredential.x-credential-instructions: Copy your user ID and API key from the Neutrino API account dashboard. The key must allow the operations you use. Connection testing consumes an IP Info request and proves API reachability.

content.description: The HTML content. This can be either a URL to load from, a file upload (multipart/form-data) or an HTML content string
content.title: Content

output-type.description:
The level of sanitization, possible values are:
plain-text: reduce the content to plain text only (no HTML tags at all)
plain-text-markdown: reduce the content to plain text only but also convert HTML links and lists into makrdown style text
simple-text: allow only very basic text formatting tags like b, em, i, strong, u
basic-html: allow advanced text formatting and hyper links
basic-html-with-images: same as basic html but also allows image tags
advanced-html: same as basic html with images but also allows many more common HTML tags like table, ul, dl, pre
output-type.title: Output-Type

NeutrinoConvertConfig.description: Convert currency and other numerical units between each other

from-type.description: The type of the value to convert from (e.g. USD)
from-type.title: From-Type

to-type.description: The type to convert to (e.g. EUR)
to-type.title: To-Type

historical-date.description: Convert using the rate on a historical date, accepted date formats are: YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, YYYY. Historical rates are stored with daily granularity so the date format YYYY-MM-DD is preferred for the highest precision. The earliest date currently possible is: 2000-01-01. If an invalid date or a date too far into the past is supplied then the API will respond with 'valid' as false and an empty 'historical-date'
historical-date.title: Historical-Date

NeutrinoFilterBadWordsConfig.description: Detect bad words, swear words and profanity in a given text

content.description: The content to scan. This can be either a URL to load from, a file upload (multipart/form-data) or an HTML content string
content.title: Content

censor-character.description: The character to use to censor out the bad words found
censor-character.title: Censor-Character

catalog.description:
Which catalog of bad words to use, we currently maintain two bad word catalogs:
  • strict - the largest database of bad words which includes profanity, obscenity, sexual, rude, cuss, dirty, swear and objectionable words and phrases. This catalog is suitable for environments of all ages including educational or children's content
  • obscene - like the strict catalog but does not include any mild profanities, idiomatic phrases or words which are considered formal terminology. This catalog is suitable for adult environments where certain types of bad words are considered OK
catalog.title: Catalog

NeutrinoFilterBadWordsConfig.title: NeutrinoFilterBadWordsConfig

NeutrinoGetGeocodeAddressConfig.description: Geocode an address, partial address or the name of a place

address.description: The full address, partial address or name of a place to try and locate. Comma separated address components are preferred.
address.title: Address

house-number.description: The house/building number to locate (for structured address searches)
house-number.title: House-Number

street.description: The street/road name to locate (for structured address searches)
street.title: Street

city.description: The city/town name to locate (for structured address searches)

county.description: The county/region name to locate (for structured address searches)

state.description: The state name to locate (for structured address searches)

postal-code.description: The postal code to locate (for structured address searches)

country-code.description: Prefer results from this country code (the default is no country bias)
country-code.title: Country-Code

country-codes.description: Prefer results from this list of country codes (space or comma separated values). Preference is in the order supplied, you can use the 'country-code' parameter to also set a dynamic or user supplied country code which takes precedence

auto-complete.description: Enable auto-complete for search-as-you-type and search suggestions. Auto-complete works best with 'fuzzy-search' disabled for the fastest response times but can be combined if required

fuzzy-search.description: If no matches are found for the given address, start performing a recursive fuzzy search until a geolocation is found. This option is useful for processing user supplied input that may be incomplete or have typos and where you do not mind some potential loss in precision

NeutrinoGetUaLookupConfig.description: Parse, validate and get detailed user-agent information from a user agent string or from client hints

ua.description: The user-agent string to lookup. For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua' header or you can also pass the JSON data directly from the 'navigator.userAgentData.getHighEntropyValues()' JavaScript API
ua.title: Ua

ua-version.description: For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua-full-version' header
ua-version.title: Ua-Version

ua-platform.description: For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua-platform' header
ua-platform.title: Ua-Platform

ua-platform-version.description: For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua-platform-version' header
ua-platform-version.title: Ua-Platform-Version

ua-mobile.description: For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua-mobile' header
ua-mobile.title: Ua-Mobile

device-model.description:
For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua-model' header.
You can also use this parameter to lookup a device directly by its model name, model code or hardware code, on android you can get the model name from: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Build.html#MODEL
device-model.title: Device-Model

device-brand.description: This parameter is only used in combination with 'device-model' for direct device lookups without any user-agent data. Set this to the brand or manufacturer name, this is required for accurate device detection with ambiguous model names. On android you can get the device brand from: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/Build#MANUFACTURER

ua-arch.description: For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua-arch' header
ua-arch.title: Ua-Arch

ua-bitness.description: For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua-bitness' header
ua-bitness.title: Ua-Bitness

ua-form-factors.description: For client hints this corresponds to the 'sec-ch-ua-form-factors' header
ua-form-factors.title: Ua-Form-Factors
